lessons.title: Exercise 1.1 - Numbers up to 1,000,000
lessons.notes_html:
Try Yourself Write the place and place value of each digit in 237 112, and write it in words.

"2" is at hundred thousands place, so its place value = 2 x 100 000 = 200 000
"3" is at ten thousands place, so its place value = 3 x 10 000 = 30 000
"7" is at thousands place, so its place value = 7 x 1 000 = 7 000
"1" is at hundreds place, so its place value = 1 x 100 = 100
"1" is at tens place, so its place value = 1 x 10 = 10
"2" is at ones place, so its place value = 2 x 1 = 2

Try Yourself K-2 is 861 100 centimetres high. (a) Write it in expanded form. (b) Write the place value of each digit. (c) Write this height in words.

(a) Expanded form: 800 000 + 60 000 + 1 000 + 100.
(b) Place values:
"8" is at hundred thousands place, so its place value = 8 x 100 000 = 800 000
"6" is at ten thousands place, so its place value = 6 x 10 000 = 60 000
"1" is at thousands place, so its place value = 1 x 1 000 = 1 000
"1" is at hundreds place, so its place value = 1 x 100 = 100
"0" is at tens place, so its place value = 0 x 10 = 0
"0" is at ones place, so its place value = 0 x 1 = 0
(c) In words: Eight hundred sixty-one thousand one hundred.

Try Yourself What number am I? I am a 6-digit number. My tens place digit is 5. My ten thousands place digit is 3 less than my tens digit. My ones place digit is the greatest 1-digit even number. My thousands place digit is 3 times my ten thousands place digit. My greatest place value digit is the sum of my tens place digit and my ten thousands place digit. My hundreds place digit is the ones digit of the smallest 2-digit number.

Step 1: Tens digit = 5.
Step 2: Ten thousands digit = 5 - 3 = 2.
Step 3: Ones digit = greatest 1-digit even number = 8.
Step 4: Thousands digit = 3 x 2 = 6.
Step 5: Hundred thousands digit = 5 + 2 = 7.
Step 6: Hundreds digit = ones digit of 10 = 0.
Answer: The number is 726 058.

Q5. According to 2017 census, the population of Islamabad is 114 825. (a) Write it in words. (b) Write it in expanded form. (c) Write the place of each digit in it.

(b) Expanded form: 100 000 + 10 000 + 4 000 + 800 + 20 + 5.
(c) Places: 1 is at hundred thousands, 1 is at ten thousands, 4 is at thousands, 8 is at hundreds, 2 is at tens, 5 is at ones.

Q6. The speed of light in vacuum is 299 792 kilometres per second. (a) Write it in words. (b) Write it in expanded form. (c) Write the place of each digit in it.

(a) In words: Two hundred ninety-nine thousand seven hundred ninety-two.
(b) Expanded form: 200 000 + 90 000 + 9 000 + 700 + 90 + 2.
(c) Places: 2 is at hundred thousands, 9 is at ten thousands, 9 is at thousands, 7 is at hundreds, 9 is at tens, 2 is at ones.

mcqs.q: In 237 112, what is the place value of the digit 2?
mcqs.why: The digit 2 is at the hundred thousands place, so its place value is 2 x 100 000 = 200 000.

mcqs.q: How is 290 014 written in words?
options: Two hundred ninety thousand four hundred
mcqs.why: 290 014 is read in groups: 290 thousand and 14, so it is two hundred ninety thousand fourteen.

mcqs.q: What is the expanded form of 600 900?
mcqs.why: In 600 900 only two digits are non-zero: 600 900 = 600 000 + 900, so the expanded form is 600 000 + 900.

mcqs.q: In 980 714, what is the place value of the digit 8?
mcqs.why: The digit 8 is at the ten thousands place, so its place value is 8 x 10 000 = 80 000.

mcqs.q: Which number matches the words 'Eight hundred seven thousand eight hundred'?
mcqs.why: Eight hundred seven thousand is 807 000 and eight hundred is 800, and 807 000 + 800 = 807 800.

mcqs.q: The population of Islamabad is 114 825. What is its expanded form?
mcqs.why: Each digit is written with its place value: 114 825 = 100 000 + 10 000 + 4 000 + 800 + 20 + 5.

mcqs.q: The speed of light is 299 792 km per second. What is the place value of the digit 7?
mcqs.why: In 299 792 the digit 7 is at the hundreds place, so its place value is 7 x 100 = 700.

mcqs.q: A 6-digit number has tens digit 5, ten thousands digit 3 less than the tens digit, ones digit 8, thousands digit 3 times the ten thousands digit, hundred thousands digit equal to the sum of the tens and ten thousands digits, and hundreds digit 0. What is the number?
mcqs.why: Ten thousands digit: 5 - 3 = 2. Thousands digit: 3 x 2 = 6. Hundred thousands digit: 5 + 2 = 7. So the number is 726 058.

mcqs.q: K-2 is 861 100 centimetres high. How is this height written in words?
options: Eight hundred sixty-one thousand one hundred
Eight hundred sixty-one thousand one thousand
Eight hundred sixty thousand one hundred
mcqs.why: 861 100 is read as 861 thousand and 100, so it is eight hundred sixty-one thousand one hundred.

mcqs.q: In 817 656, what is the place value of the last digit 6?
mcqs.why: The last digit 6 is at the ones place, so its place value is 6 x 1 = 6.

lessons.notes_html:
Try Yourself Ahad planted a plant in a pot. Its height increases by 4 cm daily. If on Monday the height was 12 cm, on which day will the plant be 36 cm high?

Height needed = 36 - 12 = 24 cm more.
Days needed = 24 / 4 = 6 days after Monday.
Monday + 6 days = Sunday.
The plant will be 36 cm high on Sunday.

Try Yourself Nida wants to plant 12 rose plants and 18 jasmine plants in rows in her home garden. If she wants to plant the same type of plant in one row, find the maximum number of plants that can be grown in one row.

Prime factorization of 12 = 2 x 2 x 3.
Prime factorization of 18 = 2 x 3 x 3.
Common prime factors: 2 x 3 = 6.
Answer: HCF = 6.
Maximum plants in one row = 6.

Worked example Sara has two pieces of ribbon whose lengths are 18 cm and 24 cm. She wants to cut the ribbon into smaller pieces of equal length without any ribbon left. What will be the greatest possible length of each piece?

Prime factorization of 18 = 2 x 3 x 3.
Prime factorization of 24 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3.
Common prime factors: 2 x 3 = 6.
Answer: HCF = 6.
Greatest possible length of each piece = 6 cm.

Worked example Find the HCF of 12, 30 and 44 by using prime factorization.

Prime factorization of 12 = 2 x 2 x 3.

Answer: HCF = 2.

Worked example Hammad has 36 red pencils and 54 blue pencils. He wants to put these pencils in boxes such that every box has an equal number of pencils of the same colour. What will be the maximum number of pencils in each box?

Prime factorization of 54 = 2 x 3 x 3 x 3.
Division method steps:
54 = 36 x 1 + 18
36 = 18 x 2 + 0
The last divisor is 18, so the HCF = 18.
Answer: HCF = 18.
Maximum pencils in each box = 18.

LCM of 35, 60, 75

Answer: LCM = 2 100.

LCM of 7, 21, 49

Prime factorization of 49 = 7 x 7.
Answer: LCM = 147.

LCM of 25, 45, 95

Prime factorization of 25 = 5 x 5.
Prime factorization of 45 = 3 x 3 x 5.

Answer: LCM = 4 275.

LCM of 16, 32, 48

Prime factorization of 32 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2.

Answer: LCM = 96.

LCM of 28, 32, 40

Q3. Find the minimum length of the ribbon which can completely be cut into pieces of length 45 cm, 75 cm and 85 cm without any left over.

Prime factorization of 45 = 3 x 3 x 5.
Prime factorization of 75 = 3 x 5 x 5.
Prime factorization of 85 = 5 x 17.
Answer: LCM = 3 825.

Q4. Find the smallest number that can completely be divided by 42, 38 and 16 without leaving any remainder.

Prime factorization of 42 = 2 x 3 x 7.

Q5. The tour buses for Badshahi Masjid leave the station every 25 minutes, for the interior city every 15 minutes and for the zoo every 30 minutes. If the three buses leave the station simultaneously at 11:05 a.m., find out the time when the three buses will next leave the station simultaneously?

Prime factorization of 25 = 5 x 5.
Prime factorization of 15 = 3 x 5.
Prime factorization of 30 = 2 x 3 x 5.
Answer: LCM = 150.

11:05 a.m. + 2 hours 30 minutes = 1:35 p.m.
The three buses will next leave together at 1:35 p.m.

Q6. Boxes having 22 centimetre, 35 centimetre and 50 centimetre height respectively are to be stacked next to each other. What is the shortest possible height at which the three types of boxes will be at the same height?

Answer: LCM = 3 850.

Q7. Students of grade 5 have Mathematics test after every 3 days, English test after every 6 days and Science test after every 9 days. If all the three tests were conducted today, find out when will the three tests be conducted next on the same day?

mcqs.q: Grade 4 students visit the science laboratory every 8 days and Grade 5 students every 12 days. If both visited today, after how many days will they visit together again?
mcqs.why: The first common multiple of 8 and 12 is the LCM. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24 and multiples of 12: 12, 24, so the LCM is 24 days.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 16, 30 and 64?
mcqs.why: 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2, 30 = 2 x 3 x 5 and 64 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2. Taking the highest powers gives 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 = 960.

mcqs.q: Ali, Ahmad and Umar exercise after every 10, 18 and 20 days. If they all exercise today, after how many days will they exercise together again?
mcqs.why: The LCM of 10, 18 and 20 is 180, so they will exercise together again on the 180th day.

mcqs.q: Packets hold 25 masks, 20 pairs of gloves and 5 sanitizer bottles. The LCM of 25, 20 and 5 is 100 items of each kind. How many packets of masks are needed to get 100 masks?
mcqs.why: Each packet has 25 masks, so the packets needed are 100 / 25 = 4 packets.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 12 and 80?
mcqs.why: 12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 80 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 5. Taking the highest powers gives 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 = 240.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 9, 18 and 27?
mcqs.why: 9 = 3 x 3, 18 = 2 x 3 x 3 and 27 = 3 x 3 x 3. Taking the highest powers gives 2 x 3 x 3 x 3 = 54.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 20, 60 and 75?
mcqs.why: 20 = 2 x 2 x 5, 60 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 and 75 = 3 x 5 x 5. Taking the highest powers gives 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 x 5 = 300.

mcqs.q: Buses for three places leave a station every 25, 15 and 30 minutes. They all leave together at 11:05 a.m. When will they next leave together?
mcqs.why: The LCM of 25, 15 and 30 is 150 minutes, which is 2 hours 30 minutes. 11:05 a.m. + 2 hours 30 minutes = 1:35 p.m.

mcqs.q: Grade 5 has a Mathematics test every 3 days, an English test every 6 days and a Science test every 9 days. All three tests were held today. After how many days will all three fall on the same day again?
mcqs.why: The LCM of 3, 6 and 9 is 18, so the three tests will next fall on the same day after 18 days.

mcqs.q: What is the smallest number that can be divided completely by 42, 38 and 16?
mcqs.why: The smallest such number is the LCM of 42, 38 and 16. Taking the highest prime powers gives 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 7 x 19 = 6 384.

lessons.title: Exercise 1 - Addition and Subtraction of Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Worked example Yesterday we spent 1/2 hour and today we spent 3/4 hour in the computer lab. How much time have we spent altogether?

LCM of denominators = 4.
1/2 = 2/4
3/4 = 3/4
Add: 2/4 + 3/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4.
Total time spent = 1 1/4 hours.

Worked example Sidra used 1 3/4 metre red ribbon and 7/8 metre blue ribbon to decorate the gift boxes. Find the total length of the ribbon she used.

Convert the mixed fraction into improper fraction: 1 3/4 = 7/4.
LCM of denominators = 8.
7/4 = 14/8
7/8 = 7/8
Add: 14/8 + 7/8 = 21/8 = 2 5/8.
Sidra used 2 5/8 m ribbon.

Worked example Sara uses 1/2 spoon sugar and 1/3 spoon of tea to make a cup of tea. Find how much more sugar she uses than the tea.

LCM of denominators = 6.
1/2 = 3/6, 1/3 = 2/6.
Subtract: 3/6 - 2/6 = 1/6 = 1/6.
Sara uses 1/6 spoon more sugar.

Activity: Try Yourself Observe the given shapes. Write the addition sentence for them and solve. (Add the shaded parts of the shapes as fractions with the same denominator.)

Q1. Solve the following fractions (addition):

(a) 1/2 + 1/2

LCM of denominators = 2.
1/2 = 1/2
1/2 = 1/2
Add: 1/2 + 1/2 = 2/2 = 1.

(b) 5 2/3 + 2 5/7

LCM of denominators = 21.
17/3 = 119/21
19/7 = 57/21
Add: 119/21 + 57/21 = 176/21 = 8 8/21.

(c) 3 4/5 + 5/7

LCM of denominators = 35.
19/5 = 133/35
5/7 = 25/35
Add: 133/35 + 25/35 = 158/35 = 4 18/35.

(d) 4 7/10 + 3/4

LCM of denominators = 20.
47/10 = 94/20
3/4 = 15/20
Add: 94/20 + 15/20 = 109/20 = 5 9/20.

(e) 7/9 + 3/4 + 2

LCM of denominators = 36.
7/9 = 28/36
3/4 = 27/36
2 = 72/36
Add: 28/36 + 27/36 + 72/36 = 127/36 = 3 19/36.

(f) 1 3/10 + 6 7/10 + 2 3/8

LCM of denominators = 40.
13/10 = 52/40
67/10 = 268/40
19/8 = 95/40
Add: 52/40 + 268/40 + 95/40 = 415/40 = 10 3/8.

(g) 4 + 2 7/12 + 1 19/24

LCM of denominators = 24.
4 = 96/24
31/12 = 62/24
43/24 = 43/24
Add: 96/24 + 62/24 + 43/24 = 201/24 = 8 3/8.

(h) 7/8 + 4 1/4 + 15/16

LCM of denominators = 16.
7/8 = 14/16
17/4 = 68/16
15/16 = 15/16
Add: 14/16 + 68/16 + 15/16 = 97/16 = 6 1/16.

Q2. Solve the following fractions (subtraction):

(a) 1 1/2 - 1/12

LCM of denominators = 12.
3/2 = 18/12, 1/12 = 1/12.
Subtract: 18/12 - 1/12 = 17/12 = 1 5/12.

(b) 2 8/9 - 1 2/3

LCM of denominators = 9.
26/9 = 26/9, 5/3 = 15/9.
Subtract: 26/9 - 15/9 = 11/9 = 1 2/9.

(c) 3 5/14 - 1 2/21

LCM of denominators = 42.
47/14 = 141/42, 23/21 = 46/42.
Subtract: 141/42 - 46/42 = 95/42 = 2 11/42.

(d) 5/6 - 6/11

LCM of denominators = 66.
5/6 = 55/66, 6/11 = 36/66.
Subtract: 55/66 - 36/66 = 19/66 = 19/66.

(e) 4 1/6 - 17/18

LCM of denominators = 18.
25/6 = 75/18, 17/18 = 17/18.
Subtract: 75/18 - 17/18 = 58/18 = 3 2/9.

(f) 1 3/4 - 4/5

LCM of denominators = 20.
7/4 = 35/20, 4/5 = 16/20.
Subtract: 35/20 - 16/20 = 19/20 = 19/20.

(g) 2 13/24 - 2/9

LCM of denominators = 72.
61/24 = 183/72, 2/9 = 16/72.
Subtract: 183/72 - 16/72 = 167/72 = 2 23/72.

(h) 5 1/8 - 1/3

LCM of denominators = 24.
41/8 = 123/24, 1/3 = 8/24.
Subtract: 123/24 - 8/24 = 115/24 = 4 19/24.

Q3. To practice for a marathon, Raheel ran 1/4 km on Monday, 7/8 km on Tuesday and 15/6 km on Wednesday. Find out how many kilometres did he run in three days?

LCM of denominators = 8.
1/4 = 2/8
7/8 = 7/8
5/2 = 20/8
Add: 2/8 + 7/8 + 20/8 = 29/8 = 3 5/8.
Raheel ran 3 5/8 km in three days.

Q4. Saad spent 2 1/2 hours for the preparation of Mathematics test and 1 1/4 hours for the preparation of Urdu test. Find: (a) in which subject did he spend more time and by how much? (b) how much time did he spend altogether?

(a) More time in Mathematics:
LCM of denominators = 4.
5/2 = 10/4, 5/4 = 5/4.
Subtract: 10/4 - 5/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4.
(b) Total time:
LCM of denominators = 4.
5/2 = 10/4
5/4 = 5/4
Add: 10/4 + 5/4 = 15/4 = 3 3/4.
Saad spent 1 1/4 hours more in Mathematics, and 3 3/4 hours altogether.

Q5. An electrician has 18 8/9 m of wire. If he uses 2/9 m and 2 1/3 m in two rooms, then find: (a) how much wire did he use altogether? (b) how much wire is left?

(a) Wire used:
LCM of denominators = 9.
2/9 = 2/9
7/3 = 21/9
Add: 2/9 + 21/9 = 23/9 = 2 5/9.
(b) Wire left:
LCM of denominators = 9.
170/9 = 170/9, 23/9 = 23/9.
Subtract: 170/9 - 23/9 = 147/9 = 16 1/3.
He used 2 5/9 m wire altogether, and 16 1/3 m wire is left.

lessons.title: Exercise 2 - Multiplication and Division of Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Worked example Ibrahim takes 3/4 hours daily to complete his homework. How much time does he spend on his homework in a week?

3/4 x 7 = 21/4 = 5 1/4 hours.
Ibrahim spends 5 1/4 hours on homework in a week.

Worked example Rabia completed one round of the park and covered a distance of 2 1/2 km. If she took 3 rounds of the park, how much distance did she cover?

2 1/2 x 3 = 5/2 x 3 = 15/2 = 7 1/2 km.
Rabia covered 7 1/2 km in 3 rounds.

Worked example For an experiment, I have to pour 7 litres of water in glasses with a capacity of 1/3 litres. Find the number of glasses to fill this quantity of water.

7 / (1/3) = 7 x 3 = 21 glasses.
I will need 21 glasses.

Q1. Solve the following and represent with figures:

(a) 1/2 x 12 (represent with figures)

1/2 x 12 = 6 = 6. (Draw 12 shapes, shade 1/2 of each, and count the shaded parts.)

(b) 5/9 x 7 (represent with figures)

5/9 x 7 = 35/9 = 3 8/9. (Draw 7 shapes, shade 5/9 of each, and count the shaded parts.)

(c) 6/7 x 3 (represent with figures)

6/7 x 3 = 18/7 = 2 4/7. (Draw 3 shapes, shade 6/7 of each, and count the shaded parts.)

(d) 3/4 x 4 (represent with figures)

3/4 x 4 = 3 = 3. (Draw 4 shapes, shade 3/4 of each, and count the shaded parts.)

(e) 2/3 x 5 (represent with figures)

2/3 x 5 = 10/3 = 3 1/3. (Draw 5 shapes, shade 2/3 of each, and count the shaded parts.)

(f) 5/6 x 9 (represent with figures)

5/6 x 9 = 15/2 = 7 1/2. (Draw 9 shapes, shade 5/6 of each, and count the shaded parts.)

Q2. Solve the following (multiplication):

(a) 4/5 x 1/4

Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator: 4/5 x 1/4 = 1/5 = 1/5.

(b) 3/7 x 7/9

Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator: 3/7 x 7/9 = 1/3 = 1/3.

(c) 1 2/3 x 3 3/4

Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator: 5/3 x 15/4 = 25/4 = 6 1/4.

(d) 29/30 x 1/5 x 1/2

Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator: 29/30 x 1/5 x 1/2 = 29/300 = 29/300.

(e) 2/7 x 4/5 x 3/7

Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator: 2/7 x 4/5 x 3/7 = 24/245 = 24/245.

(f) 1 1/14 x 1/4 x 2/3

Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator: 15/14 x 1/4 x 2/3 = 5/28 = 5/28.

(g) 1 3/5 x 2 3/7 x 3 3/4

Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator: 8/5 x 17/7 x 15/4 = 102/7 = 14 4/7.

(h) 5 2/7 x 8 2/5 x 9 3/11

Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator: 37/7 x 42/5 x 102/11 = 22644/55 = 411 39/55.

(i) 9 1/9 x 10 1/3 x 5 1/2

Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator: 82/9 x 31/3 x 11/2 = 13981/27 = 517 22/27.

Q3. Solve the following (division):

(a) 1/3 / 2/9

Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal: 1/3 / 2/9 = 1/3 x 9/2 = 3/2 = 1 1/2.

(b) 3/25 / 1/5

Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal: 3/25 / 1/5 = 3/25 x 5 = 3/5 = 3/5.

(c) 1/12 / 7/20

Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal: 1/12 / 7/20 = 1/12 x 20/7 = 5/21 = 5/21.

(d) 2 29/30 / 4 1/5

Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal: 89/30 / 21/5 = 89/30 x 5/21 = 89/126 = 89/126.

(e) 5 5/9 / 9 6/7

Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal: 50/9 / 69/7 = 50/9 x 7/69 = 350/621 = 350/621.

(f) 6 15/16 / 7 1/2

Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal: 111/16 / 15/2 = 111/16 x 2/15 = 37/40 = 37/40.

(g) 2 5/6 / 4 2/9

Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal: 17/6 / 38/9 = 17/6 x 9/38 = 51/76 = 51/76.

(h) 3 1/2 / 4/9

Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal: 7/2 / 4/9 = 7/2 x 9/4 = 63/8 = 7 7/8.

(i) 1/7 / 2 6/7

Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal: 1/7 / 20/7 = 1/7 x 7/20 = 1/20 = 1/20.

Q4. If 5 1/2 m of cloth is used to stitch one dress, how much cloth will be used to stitch 7 such dresses?

5 1/2 x 7 = 11/2 x 7 = 77/2 = 38 1/2 m.
38 1/2 m cloth will be used for 7 dresses.

Q5. Hina ate 1/2 part of a cake. If there were 8 pieces of cake, how many pieces did Hina eat?

1/2 x 8 = 4.
Hina ate 4 pieces.

Q6. Nida had 3/12 of a pizza. She gave 1/8 of it to her friend Madeeha. Find out what part of the whole pizza did Madeeha get?

3/12 x 1/8 = 3/96 = 1/32.
Madeeha got 1/32 part of the whole pizza.

Q7. To decorate the classroom, Hassan used ribbons of two colours. The length of blue ribbon is 5 7/8 metres. The length of red ribbon is 2/3 of the length of blue ribbon. (a) What is the length of red ribbon? (b) Find the total length of both ribbons.

(a) Red ribbon = 2/3 x 47/8 = 94/24 = 47/12 = 3 11/12 m.
(b) Total length:
LCM of denominators = 24.
47/8 = 141/24
47/12 = 94/24
Add: 141/24 + 94/24 = 235/24 = 9 19/24.
Red ribbon = 3 11/12 m, total length = 9 19/24 m.

Q8. 44 1/6 kilogram sugar is to be packed in 4 5/12 kilogram packets. Find: (a) in how many packets sugar will be packed? (b) how much sugar will be there in 9 packets of mass 4 5/12 kilograms?

(a) Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal: 265/6 / 53/12 = 265/6 x 12/53 = 10 = 10.
Sugar will be packed in 10 packets.
(b) 9 x 53/12 = 477/12 = 159/4 = 39 3/4 kg.
9 packets contain 39 3/4 kg sugar.

lessons.title: Exercise 1 - Comparing and Ordering Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
Try Yourself Compare by using the correct symbol: (i) 0.30 [ ] 0.3 (ii) 1.02 [ ] 1.22 (iii) 1.31 [ ] 1.3 (iv) 5.13 [ ] 5.03.

mcqs.q: Which statement about 0.30 and 0.3 is correct?
mcqs.why: Putting a 0 at the right of a decimal does not change its value, so 0.30 = 0.3.

mcqs.q: Which symbol correctly compares 1.02 and 1.22?
mcqs.why: Both numbers have whole part 1, but at the tenths place 0 is less than 2, so 1.02 < 1.22.

mcqs.q: Which is greater, 71.2 or 71.02?
mcqs.why: 71.2 has 2 in the tenths place while 71.02 has 0 in the tenths place. More tenths means a greater number, so 71.2 is greater than 71.02.

mcqs.q: Which statement about 4.8 and 4.80 is correct?
mcqs.why: A zero at the right end of a decimal does not change its value, so 4.8 = 4.80.

mcqs.q: Which is the smallest of 8.56, 8.06, 8.5, 8.52, 8.51 and 8.05?
mcqs.why: All start with 8.0 or 8.5; the smallest hundredths value is in 8.05, which begins the ascending order 8.05, 8.06, 8.5, 8.51, 8.52, 8.56.

mcqs.q: Which is the greatest of 3.4, 3.54, 3.55, 3.45, 3.14 and 3.04?
mcqs.why: Comparing the hundredths digits, 3.55 is the largest; the ascending order ends with 3.54, 3.55.

mcqs.q: Which is the greatest of 2.51, 3.31, 2.47, 3.81 and 3.01?
mcqs.why: Among the numbers starting with 3, the tenths digits are 3, 8 and 0; 8 is the greatest, so 3.81 is the greatest number.

mcqs.q: Which symbol correctly compares 6.06 and 6.1?
mcqs.why: 6.06 has 0 in the tenths place while 6.1 has 1 in the tenths place. Fewer tenths means a smaller number, so 6.06 < 6.1.

lessons.title: Exercise 1 - Conversion of Units of Distance
lessons.notes_html:
Worked example Farhan participated in a cycle race. He has to cover a distance of 15 kilometres to win the race. How many metres are there in 15 kilometres?

1 km = 1 000 m, so 15 km = 15 x 1 000 = 15 000 m.

Worked example Children are going to Murree from Islamabad for a recreational trip. They cover the distance of 55 km. How many metres do they cover?

55 km = 55 x 1 000 = 55 000 m.

Try Yourself Nanga Parbat is the ninth highest mountain in the world. Its height is 8 kilometres 126 metres. What will be its height in metres?

8 km 126 m = 8 x 1 000 m + 126 m = 8 000 m + 126 m = 8 126 m.

Worked example The distance of my home to the park is 2 000 metres. Find this distance in kilometres.

2 000 m = 2 000 / 1 000 = 2 km.

Worked example Convert 9 800 metres to kilometres and metres.

9 800 m = 9 000 m + 800 m = 9 km 800 m.

Try Yourself Convert the following distances into kilometres and metres: (i) 5 000 m (ii) 2 002 m (iii) 8 976 m.

(i) 5 000 m = 5 km.
(ii) 2 002 m = 2 km 2 m.
(iii) 8 976 m = 8 km 976 m.

Worked example The height of Minar-e-Pakistan is 70 m. What will be its height in centimetres?

70 m = 70 x 100 = 7 000 cm.

Try Yourself A tree is 7.5 metres high. What will be its height in centimetres?

7.5 m = 7.5 x 100 = 750 cm.

Worked example Convert 38 m 78 cm in centimetres only.

38 m 78 cm = 38 x 100 cm + 78 cm = 3 800 cm + 78 cm = 3 878 cm.

Worked example The height of a cupboard is 200 centimetres. What will be its height in metres?

200 cm = 200 / 100 = 2 m.

Worked example Convert 585 cm into metres and centimetres.

585 cm = 500 cm + 85 cm = 5 m 85 cm.

Try Yourself Convert the following distances into metres: (i) 670 cm (ii) 409 cm (iii) 900 cm.

(i) 670 cm = 6 m 70 cm.
(ii) 409 cm = 4 m 9 cm.
(iii) 900 cm = 9 m.

Worked example The length of Anmer's lunch box is 15 cm. What will be its length in millimetres?

15 cm = 15 x 10 = 150 mm.

Try Yourself Ahmed buys a toy car which is 24 cm long. What will be its length in millimetres?

24 cm = 24 x 10 = 240 mm.

Worked example Convert 89 centimetres 44 millimetres into millimetres.

89 cm 44 mm = 89 x 10 mm + 44 mm = 890 mm + 44 mm = 934 mm.

Worked example I bought a picture frame. Its length is 60 millimetre. Find its length in centimetres.

60 mm = 60 / 10 = 6 cm.

lessons.title: Exercise 2 - Addition and Subtraction of Distance

lessons.title: Exercise 1 - Angles
lessons.notes_html:
Key facts: What is a straight angle? What is a reflex angle? What is the standard unit for measuring angles?

A straight angle measures 180 degrees.
A reflex angle is greater than 180 degrees but smaller than a complete rotation of 360 degrees.
The standard unit for measuring angles is the degree, written as degrees. One degree is 1/360 of a complete revolution.

Try Yourself How many 30 degree angles are there in a right angle?

A right angle = 90 degrees. 90 / 30 = 3.
There are three 30 degree angles in a right angle.

Try Yourself (1) How many right angles are there in a straight angle? (2) How many straight angles are there in a complete rotation?

(1) A straight angle = 180 degrees, a right angle = 90 degrees. 180 / 90 = 2 right angles.
(2) A complete rotation = 360 degrees. 360 / 180 = 2 straight angles.

Worked construction Construct an angle ABC = 285 degrees by using a protractor.

A reflex angle of 285 degrees: first subtract from 360 degrees: 360 - 285 = 75 degrees.
Draw a ray BA, place the protractor upside down on ray BA, mark a point C at 75 degrees, join B to C.
Angle ABC = 285 degrees is the required reflex angle.

Pairs of angles: What are adjacent angles? Give an example from the book.

Adjacent angles are two angles that have a common vertex and a common side, and lie on opposite sides of the common side.
Example: Angle AOB is adjacent to angle BOC. Their common arm is OB and the common vertex is O.

Pairs of angles: What are complementary angles? Give an example from the book.

Two angles are called complementary angles if their sum is 90 degrees. One angle is the complement of the other. They may be adjacent or non-adjacent.
Example: Angle AOD + Angle DOB = 45 degrees + 45 degrees = 90 degrees.

Try Yourself Can two right angles be the complementary angles of each other? Explain your answer.

No. Two right angles add to 90 + 90 = 180 degrees, not 90 degrees. So they cannot be complementary angles of each other.

Pairs of angles: What are supplementary angles? Give an example from the book.

Two angles are called supplementary angles if their sum is 180 degrees. They may be adjacent or non-adjacent.
Example: Angle AOD + Angle DOC = 100 degrees + 80 degrees = 180 degrees.

Try Yourself Can two straight angles be the supplementary angles of each other? Explain your answer.

No. Two straight angles add to 180 + 180 = 360 degrees, not 180 degrees. So they cannot be supplementary angles of each other.

lessons.title: Exercise 2 - Triangles
lessons.notes_html:
Types of triangles with respect to their sides: define equilateral, isosceles and scalene triangles.

Equilateral triangle: all three sides are equal in length. All angles of an equilateral triangle are equal to 60 degrees.
Isosceles triangle: two sides are equal in length. Two base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal in measure.
Scalene triangle: all sides are of different lengths. All angles in a scalene triangle are different in measure.

Try Yourself Is every equilateral triangle an isosceles triangle? Explain your answer.

Yes. An isosceles triangle is a triangle in which two sides are equal. An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal, so it certainly has two equal sides. Hence every equilateral triangle is also an isosceles triangle.

Types of triangles with respect to their angles: define acute angled, right angled and obtuse angled triangles, with the book's examples.

Acute angled triangle: all angles are acute (less than 90 degrees). Example: triangle FGH with angles 40, 60 and 80 degrees.
Right angled triangle: one angle is a right angle (90 degrees). Example: triangle DEF with angle E = 90 degrees.
Obtuse angled triangle: one angle is obtuse (greater than 90 degrees). Example: triangle LKM with angle K = 120 degrees.

Construction Construct a triangle EFG in which EF = 6 cm, angle E = 35 degrees and angle F = 70 degrees. Also find the measurement of the remaining angle.

Draw EF = 6 cm. Draw an angle of 35 degrees at E and an angle of 70 degrees at F. The two rays intersect at G.
Angle G = 180 - (35 + 70) = 180 - 105 = 75 degrees.
Measure EG and FG with a ruler.

Activity: Construction Construct a triangle ABC in which AB = 4 cm, angle B = 30 degrees and BC = 3 cm. Measure the remaining sides and angles with a ruler and protractor.

Activity: Q2. Identify these triangles with respect to their angles. (All angles less than 90 degrees = acute angled, one angle 90 degrees = right angled, one angle greater than 90 degrees = obtuse angled.)

Q3. Draw a triangle ABC in which angle A = 75 degrees, AB = 4 cm and angle B = 55 degrees. What is angle C?

Draw AB = 4 cm, draw 75 degrees at A and 55 degrees at B. The rays meet at C.
Angle C = 180 - (75 + 55) = 180 - 130 = 50 degrees.

Q4. Draw a triangle LMN in which angle L = 60 degrees, LM = 5.5 cm and angle M = 30 degrees. What is angle N?

Draw LM = 5.5 cm, draw 60 degrees at L and 30 degrees at M. The rays meet at N.
Angle N = 180 - (60 + 30) = 90 degrees.

Activity: Q6. Draw a triangle XYZ in which YZ = 7.3 cm, XY = 3.5 cm and angle Y = 40 degrees.

lessons.title: Exercise 3 - Quadrilaterals
lessons.notes_html:
What is a quadrilateral? Describe the six kinds taught in the book: square, rectangle, parallelogram, rhombus, trapezium and kite.

A quadrilateral is a shape with four sides and four angles.
Square: four equal sides and four right angles.
Rectangle: two pairs of parallel sides, opposite sides equal, all angles 90 degrees.
Parallelogram: two pairs of parallel sides, opposite angles equal, none of the angles a right angle.
Rhombus: all sides equal and parallel, opposite angles equal but not right angles.
Trapezium: only one pair of parallel sides.
Kite: two equal pairs of adjacent sides.

Try It Is every square a rectangle? Is every rectangle a square? Is every rhombus a parallelogram? Is every parallelogram a rhombus? Explain your answers.

Every square is a rectangle: yes, because a square has opposite sides equal and all angles 90 degrees, which is the definition of a rectangle.
Every rectangle is a square: no, because a rectangle need not have all four sides equal.
Every rhombus is a parallelogram: yes, because a rhombus has two pairs of parallel sides.
Every parallelogram is a rhombus: no, because a parallelogram need not have all sides equal.

options: Two equal pairs of adjacent sides
Only one pair of parallel sides
mcqs.why: A kite has two equal pairs of adjacent sides, that is, the equal sides are next to each other.

mcqs.q: Is every square a rectangle?
options: Yes, because a square has opposite sides equal and all angles 90 degrees
No, because a square has all sides equal
No, because rectangles have longer sides
mcqs.why: A square satisfies the definition of a rectangle: opposite sides equal and all angles 90 degrees, so every square is a rectangle.

mcqs.q: Is every rectangle a square?
options: No, because a rectangle need not have all four sides equal
Yes, because both have right angles
No, because rectangles have no parallel sides
mcqs.why: A square needs all four sides equal, but a rectangle only needs opposite sides equal, so a rectangle is not always a square.

mcqs.q: Is every rhombus a parallelogram?
options: No, because a rhombus has no parallel sides
Yes, because a rhombus has two pairs of parallel sides
Yes, because all quadrilaterals are parallelograms
mcqs.why: A parallelogram needs two pairs of parallel sides, and a rhombus has all sides parallel in pairs, so every rhombus is a parallelogram.

lessons.title: Exercise 4 - Symmetry
lessons.notes_html:
What is reflective symmetry? How many lines of symmetry do a square and a rectangle have?

Reflective symmetry: a figure has reflective symmetry about a line if folding it along that line makes one half fit exactly onto the other half. The line is called the line of symmetry.
A square has four lines of symmetry. A rectangle has two lines of symmetry.

What is rotational symmetry? What is the order of rotational symmetry in the book's examples?

Rotational symmetry: a figure has rotational symmetry if, when rotated about its centre, it looks exactly the same more than once in a complete revolution. The number of times it looks the same is the order of rotational symmetry.
The book's shape looks the same 4 times in a complete revolution (at 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees), so its order of rotational symmetry is 4.
Another figure looks the same twice, so its order is 2. A figure that looks the same only once has no rotational symmetry.

Activity: Q1. Encircle the figures which have reflective symmetry. Also draw their lines of symmetry.

Activity: Q2. Encircle the figures having rotational symmetry. Also write the order of their rotation and mark their centre of rotation.

mcqs.q: A figure has reflective symmetry about a line if:
options: It can be rotated to look the same
Folding it along the line makes one half fit exactly onto the other half
It can be divided into three equal parts
mcqs.why: In reflective symmetry, folding the figure along the line of symmetry makes one half fit exactly onto the other half.

mcqs.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
mcqs.why: A square can be folded exactly onto itself in four ways: two diagonals and two lines joining the midpoints of opposite sides, so it has 4 lines of symmetry.

mcqs.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle have?
mcqs.why: A rectangle folds exactly onto itself only along the two lines joining the midpoints of opposite sides, so it has 2 lines of symmetry.

mcqs.q: The line about which a figure has reflective symmetry is called:
mcqs.why: The fold line for reflective symmetry is called the line of symmetry of the figure.

mcqs.q: A shape in the book looks exactly the same 4 times in one complete revolution. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
mcqs.why: The order of rotational symmetry is the number of times the figure looks the same in a complete revolution, which here is 4 times.

mcqs.q: A figure looks exactly the same twice in a complete revolution. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
mcqs.why: The order of rotational symmetry counts how many times the figure looks the same in one full turn, which here is 2.

mcqs.q: A figure looks the same only once in a complete revolution. What can we say about it?
options: Its order of symmetry is 1 and it has full symmetry
It has reflective symmetry only on a diagonal
Its order of rotational symmetry is 360
mcqs.why: If a figure looks the same only once, at the full turn, it does not repeat in between, so it has no rotational symmetry.

mcqs.q: The book's shape with order 4 first looks exactly the same after a turn of how many degrees?
mcqs.why: The shape looks the same at 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees, so the first time it looks the same is after a turn of 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: Which shape has more lines of symmetry, a square or a rectangle?
mcqs.why: A square has 4 lines of symmetry while a rectangle has only 2, so the square has more lines of symmetry.

mcqs.q: When a figure, rotated about its centre, looks exactly the same more than once in a complete revolution, it has:
mcqs.why: Looking the same more than once when turned about the centre in a full revolution is called rotational symmetry.

lessons.title: Exercise 5 - Nets of 3-D Shapes
lessons.notes_html:
What is a net? Describe the nets of a cube, a cuboid and a square-based pyramid.

A net is a 2-dimensional shape which can be folded in a specific pattern to get a 3-dimensional solid. A 3-dimensional solid can have more than one possible net.
Cube: its net is made of 6 similar squares.
Cuboid: its net is made of 6 rectangles.
Square-based pyramid: its net is made of 4 triangles and 1 square.

Activity: Q1. Write the names of these figures. Also write the number and name of faces.

Activity: Q2. Identify the nets of a cube and colour them.

Activity: Q3. Observe these nets and identify the 3-D solid they are made of.

mcqs.q: What is a net of a 3-D solid?
options: A 2-dimensional shape which can be folded to get a 3-dimensional solid
A drawing of only one face of the solid
mcqs.why: A net is a 2-dimensional shape which can be folded in a specific pattern to get a 3-dimensional solid.

mcqs.q: The net of a cube is made of:
mcqs.why: A cube has 6 equal square faces, so its net is made of 6 similar squares joined in a pattern.

mcqs.q: The net of a cuboid is made of:
mcqs.why: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces, so its net is made of 6 rectangles.

mcqs.q: The net of a square-based pyramid is made of:
mcqs.why: A square-based pyramid has a square base and 4 triangular faces, so its net is made of 4 triangles and 1 square.

mcqs.q: Can one 3-dimensional solid have more than one possible net?
options: No, every solid has exactly one net
Yes, a solid can have more than one possible net
Only a cube has more than one net
Nets are not related to solids
mcqs.why: The same solid can be opened out in different ways, so a 3-dimensional solid can have more than one possible net.

mcqs.q: How many faces does a cube have?
mcqs.why: The net of a cube is made of 6 similar squares, and each square becomes one face, so a cube has 6 faces.

mcqs.q: What is the shape of the base of a square-based pyramid?
mcqs.why: As its name tells, a square-based pyramid stands on a square base, with triangles rising from its sides.

mcqs.q: How many faces does a square-based pyramid have in total?
mcqs.why: It has 4 triangular faces and 1 square face, and 4 + 1 = 5 faces in total.

mcqs.q: When a net is folded up, what do we get?
mcqs.why: A net is folded in a specific pattern to form the 3-dimensional solid whose net it is.

mcqs.q: How many rectangles are there in the net of a cuboid?
mcqs.why: A cuboid has 6 faces and all of them are rectangles, so its net contains 6 rectangles.

lessons.title: Exercise 1 - Perimeter
lessons.notes_html:
Key facts: What is area? What is perimeter? What are their units?

Area: the space covered by the surface of any 2-dimensional shape.
Perimeter: the total length of the boundary of a closed region.
Units of area: square metres (m squared) and square centimetres (cm squared).
Units of perimeter: metres (m) and centimetres (cm).

Worked example Usman has a square shaped picture frame with length of one side 22.5 cm. Find the perimeter of the frame.

Perimeter of a square = 4 x length of one side.
= 4 x 22.5 cm = 90 cm.
So, the perimeter of the picture frame is 90 cm.

Try Yourself A square shaped ground is 20 metres long. If a person takes 5 rounds of the ground, how much total distance does he cover?

Perimeter of the ground = 4 x 20 m = 80 m.
Distance in 5 rounds = 5 x 80 m = 400 m.
So, the person covers a total distance of 400 m.

Worked example A rectangular pool is 10 metres long and 7.3 metres wide. Find the perimeter of the pool.

Perimeter of rectangle = 2 (length + width).
= 2 (10 m + 7.3 m) = 2 (17.3 m) = 34.6 m.
So, the perimeter of the pool is 34.6 m.

Worked example The length of a rectangular garden is 21 metres and its width is 16 metres. If the rate of fencing is Rs. 170 per metre, find the cost of fencing around it.

Perimeter of the garden = 2 (21 + 16) = 2 (37) = 74 m.
Cost of fencing = 74 x Rs. 170 = Rs. 12,580.
So, the cost of fencing is Rs. 12,580.

Try Yourself The perimeter of a rectangular field is 66 metres. If the length of this field is 15 metres, find the width of the field. Also find the cost of putting barbed wire around the field if the rate is Rs. 90 per metre.

Perimeter = 2 (length + width).
66 = 2 (15 + width).
66 = 30 + 2 x width.
2 x width = 66 - 30 = 36.
Width = 36 / 2 = 18 m.
Cost of barbed wire = 66 x Rs. 90 = Rs. 5,940.

Umair drew a graph of monthly average temperature for the first 5 months of 2020. The table is: January 18 degrees C, February 19 degrees C, March 21 degrees C, April 24 degrees C, May 28 degrees C. Is this graph correct? If not, then identify the mistake and correct it.

lessons.title: Exercise 1 - Average
lessons.notes_html:
Key fact: How do we find the average of given quantities?

To find the average of the given quantities, we find the sum of the quantities and divide this sum by the number of quantities.
Average = Sum of quantities / Number of quantities.

Worked example I collected 16 seashells, my brother collected 12 seashells and my sister collected 11 seashells. How can we divide these seashells equally among us?

Total number of seashells = 16 + 12 + 11 = 39.
Number of persons = 3.
Number of seashells each person will get = 39 / 3 = 13.
Every person will get 13 seashells. So, 13 is the average of 16, 12 and 11.

Try Yourself Find the average of 13, 34, 16 and 28.

Sum = 13 + 34 + 16 + 28 = 91.
Number of quantities = 4.
Average = 91 / 4 = 22.75.

Worked example The length of 5 ropes is 2.4 m, 0.9 m, 1.6 m, 4.4 m and 3 m respectively. Find the average length of these ropes.

Sum of the lengths = 2.4 + 0.9 + 1.6 + 4.4 + 3 = 12.3 m.
Number of ropes = 5.
Average = 12.3 / 5 = 2.46 m.
So, the average length of the rope is 2.46 m.

Worked example In the annual exams, Ali got an average of 78 marks in 7 subjects. Find the total marks he got.

Total marks obtained = Average marks obtained x Number of subjects.
= 78 x 7 = 546.
So, Ali got 546 marks in 7 subjects.

Try Yourself Find the average of 11, 23, 37, 55 and 82.

Sum = 11 + 23 + 37 + 55 + 82 = 208.
Number of quantities = 5.
Average = 208 / 5 = 41.6.

Try Yourself If the sum of quantities is 1,840 and their average is 115, then find the number of quantities.

Number of quantities = Sum of quantities / Average.
= 1,840 / 115 = 16.

Try Yourself If the average of 40 quantities is 215, then find the sum of the quantities.

Sum of quantities = Average x Number of quantities.
= 215 x 40 = 8,600.

Try Yourself Challenge Find the number of quantities, if their sum is 5,200 and their average is 650.

Number of quantities = Sum / Average = 5,200 / 650 = 8.

Try Yourself Challenge Yousaf took 4 mathematics tests in 4 weeks. The average marks he got in these 4 tests is 62. If he scored 80 marks in the test taken on the fifth week, find out the new average of his total marks for the five weeks overall.

Total marks in 4 tests = 62 x 4 = 248.
Total marks in 5 tests = 248 + 80 = 328.
New average = 328 / 5 = 65.6.

Q5. On an average, Maryam baked 27 cakes for a bakery in 11 months. What is the total number of cakes that she baked?

Total cakes = 27 x 11 = 297.

Q6. A factory hired a total of 1,240 labourers in 4 years. Find the average number of labourers hired in a year.

Average = 1,240 / 4 = 310 labourers per year.

Q7. The runs scored by the students of a class in a cricket match are given below: Aimen 21, Haniya 52, Marwa 54, Sara 33, Nadia 37, Saba 47, Amna 28. Find the average runs of the students.

Sum = 21 + 52 + 54 + 33 + 37 + 47 + 28 = 272.
Number of students = 7.
Average = 272 / 7 = 38.86 runs (approximately).

mcqs.q: How do we find the average of given quantities?
options: Divide the number of quantities by their sum
Add the quantities and divide the sum by the number of quantities
mcqs.why: Average = Sum of quantities / Number of quantities: first add all the quantities, then divide by how many quantities there are.

mcqs.q: Three children collected 16, 12 and 11 seashells. If they share them equally, how many seashells does each get?
mcqs.why: Total seashells: 16 + 12 + 11 = 39. Shared among 3 persons: 39 / 3 = 13 seashells each.

Ali got an average of 78 marks in 7 subjects. What are his total marks?
mcqs.why: Total marks = Average x Number of subjects, and 78 x 7 = 546 marks.

mcqs.q: The sum of some quantities is 1,840 and their average is 115. How many quantities are there?
mcqs.why: Number of quantities = Sum / Average, and 1840 / 115 = 16 quantities.

mcqs.q: Yousaf's average in 4 tests is 62. He scores 80 in the fifth test. What is his new average for the 5 tests?
mcqs.why: Marks in 4 tests: 62 x 4 = 248. Total for 5 tests: 248 + 80 = 328. New average: 328 / 5 = 65.6.

mcqs.q: Munir recites 9, 11, 12, 10 and 8 Ayah in 5 days. What is the average number of Ayah she recites in one day?
mcqs.why: Total Ayah: 9 + 11 + 12 + 10 + 8 = 50. Average per day: 50 / 5 = 10 Ayah.

mcqs.q: Saad has 16 pencils, Amna 20, Sara 15 and Ahmad 9. What is the average number of pencils?
mcqs.why: Total pencils: 16 + 20 + 15 + 9 = 60. Average over 4 children: 60 / 4 = 15 pencils.

lessons.title: Exercise 2 - Bar Graphs
lessons.notes_html:
Drawing a bar graph: The table shows the marks obtained out of 10 marks in the Mathematics test during the last 4 months: September 8, October 6, November 10, December 9. What is the procedure to draw the bar graph?

Mark the horizontal line as X-axis and the vertical line as Y-axis.
Write the names of the months on the X-axis and the marks obtained on the Y-axis.
One square on the Y-axis represents 1 mark.
8 marks were obtained in September, so colour 8 squares along the Y-axis. Similarly, 6 marks in October, 10 marks in November and 9 marks in December.
In a bar graph, the width of each bar is the same. The bar graph given above is a vertical bar graph. Similarly, we can draw a horizontal bar graph.

Horizontal bar graph: The table shows the number of cars of different colours in a car parking during a month: Blue 80, Black 65, Grey 90, Red 75. Represent this data in a horizontal bar graph.

Mark the horizontal line as X-axis and the vertical line as Y-axis.
Write the number of cars on the X-axis and the colours of cars on the Y-axis.
One square on the X-axis represents 10 cars.
Draw the bars: Blue 80 (8 squares), Black 65 (6.5 squares), Grey 90 (9 squares), Red 75 (7.5 squares).

Reading a bar graph: The bar graph shows the number of flowers that bloomed in Huma's garden during five weeks. Read the graph.

6 flowers bloomed during the first week.
4 flowers bloomed during the second week.
3 flowers bloomed during the third week.
2 flowers bloomed during the fourth week.
7 flowers bloomed during the fifth week.
The maximum flowers bloomed during the fifth week.
The minimum flowers bloomed during the fourth week.

Reading a bar graph: The bar graph shows shoe production at a factory. In which year did the factory produce the most pairs of shoes? In which year the least? In which years did the factory make 20,000 pairs of shoes? How many less pairs of shoes were produced in 2011 than in 2015? In which 2 years is the difference in the number of shoes 10,000? How many pairs of shoes did the factory produce in these 5 years?

The factory produced the most pairs of shoes in 2015 (25,000 pairs).
The factory produced the least pairs of shoes in 2013 (15,000 pairs).
The factory made 20,000 pairs of shoes in 2011 and 2012.
25,000 - 20,000 = 5,000 fewer pairs of shoes were produced in 2011 than in 2015.
The difference is 10,000 between 2013 (15,000) and 2015 (25,000).
Total in 5 years = 20,000 + 20,000 + 15,000 + 22,500 + 25,000 = 102,500 pairs of shoes.

Activity: Q2. The statistics of patients visiting a hospital during 5 months is given below: February 2, March 6, April 10, May 12, June 15. Draw a vertical bar graph of the given data.

Q5. Study the graph (Transportation used for going to school: Bus 100, Rickshaw 60, Car 70, Motorbike 20, Walk 80) and answer: (a) How many students come to school by car? (b) Is the number of students coming to school on motorbikes less than those coming by rickshaw? If yes, then how much less? (c) Which means of transport do the most students use and what is the number of students coming to school by this means of transport? (d) What is the total number of students coming by car, rickshaw and bus altogether? (e) Tell the number of students coming to school on foot.

(a) 70 students come to school by car.
(b) Yes, motorbike (20) is less than rickshaw (60) by 60 - 20 = 40 students.
(c) The most students use the bus: 100 students.
(d) Car + Rickshaw + Bus = 70 + 60 + 100 = 230 students.
(e) 80 students come to school on foot (Walk).

Q6. Study the graph (Pet animals: Cat 9, Goat 4, Cow 8, Buffalo 7) and answer: (a) How many students have cat as a pet? (b) How many students have goat as a pet? (c) Which is the most popular pet? (d) In total, how many students have a pet at home? (e) If the total number of students in the class is 35, find out how many students do not have any pets in their home?

(a) 9 students have cat as a pet.
(b) 4 students have goat as a pet.
(c) Cat is the most popular pet (9 students).
(d) Total students with a pet = 9 + 4 + 8 + 7 = 28.
(e) Students without pets = 35 - 28 = 7.

mcqs.q: In a bar graph, what can we say about the width of the bars?
options: Each bar has a different width
The width of each bar is the same
mcqs.why: In a bar graph the width of each bar is the same; only the length or height of the bar changes with the value.

mcqs.q: A table shows Mathematics test marks out of 10 for four months: September 8, October 6, November 10, December 9. How many marks were obtained in November?
mcqs.why: The table gives November's marks as 10 out of 10, so the November bar is coloured up to 10 squares.

mcqs.q: In the horizontal bar graph of car colours, one square on the X-axis represents how many cars?
mcqs.why: The scale of that graph is one square = 10 cars, so the bar lengths are counted in tens of cars.

mcqs.q: There are 80 blue cars. With one square representing 10 cars, how many squares long is the bar for blue cars?
mcqs.why: Number of squares = 80 / 10 = 8, so the blue bar is drawn 8 squares long.

mcqs.q: In Huma's garden graph, during which week did the maximum number of flowers bloom?
mcqs.why: The weeks have 6, 4, 3, 2 and 7 flowers; the largest number, 7 flowers, bloomed during the fifth week.

mcqs.q: In Huma's garden graph, during which week did the minimum number of flowers bloom?
mcqs.why: The weeks have 6, 4, 3, 2 and 7 flowers; the smallest number, 2 flowers, bloomed during the fourth week.

mcqs.q: The shoe factory graph shows production of 20,000 pairs in 2011 and 2012, 15,000 in 2013, 22,500 in 2014 and 25,000 in 2015. In which year did the factory produce the most pairs?
mcqs.why: The greatest value on the graph is 25,000 pairs, which was produced in 2015.

mcqs.q: How many fewer pairs of shoes were produced in 2011 than in 2015?
mcqs.why: In 2015 the factory made 25,000 pairs and in 2011 it made 20,000 pairs, and 25 000 - 20 000 = 5 000 fewer pairs in 2011.

mcqs.q: The transport graph shows Bus 100, Rickshaw 60, Car 70, Motorbike 20 and Walk 80 students. Which means of transport do the most students use?
mcqs.why: The largest value on the graph is 100 students, which is for the bus, so the most students come by bus.

mcqs.q: In the pet graph, 9 students have a cat, 4 a goat, 8 a cow and 7 a buffalo. The class has 35 students. How many students have no pet?
mcqs.why: Students with a pet: 9 + 4 + 8 + 7 = 28. Students without a pet: 35 - 28 = 7.
